articles.title: Yemen's Houthis to target US interests if supports Saudi strikes
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Yemen's Houthis to target US interests if it supports Saudi-led strikes
A Houthi military adviser said that the group would attack US interests in the region if Washington intervenes in Yemen's war in support of Saudi Arabia or tries to unblock the Bab al-Mandeb strait.
The Iran-backed Houthis seized control of the narrow shipping lane, gateway to the Red Sea, this month, while Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested American and international military assistance against them.
"If America dares to intervene militarily with its fleets or tries to take control of Bab al-Mandeb, it is a red line for them and anyone else... we will fight over it," military adviser Abed Mohammed al-Thawr told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday.
The Houthi blockade has shaken Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, which was already hit by Tehran's strangehold on the strategic Strait of Hormuz as part of its war with the United States.
The pro-Iran Houthis dislodged Saudi-backed government forces from Yemen's Red Sea coast in fighting that left hundreds dead. Houthi drones and missiles have also targeted Saudi sites, including the capital Riyadh for the first time in years.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman requested help from US President Donald Trump in fighting the Houthis, according to US reports. Yemen's government also made the request, a well-placed source told AFP.
The Houthis say Saudi Arabia has conducted hundreds of strikes in Yemen since fighting resumed in July, effectively ending a four-year truce.
'Iron fist'
"If America gambles on supporting Saudi Arabia with airstrikes or air support... We will consider any American interests around us to be targets and we will not exclude anything," Thawr told AFP, adding that they will "close Bab al-Mandeb completely to American ships".
While the Yemen war predates the US-Iran war by years, renewed fighting in Yemen pits allies of Washington and Tehran against each other while the two foes are stalemated in the Gulf.
Thawr denied receiving directives from Iran, but said they are "one alliance and one body".
"Iran is a friendly, allied, and brotherly country to us, but it does not direct us. We are independent in our decisions and in our sovereignty," he said.
The United Nations on Tuesday said the number of people displaced could swell from over 130,000 today to more than 230,000 in the coming months.
"As long as Saudi Arabia insists on and continues killing our country and striking our people, we will strike with an iron fist," Thawr said. "We possess sufficient capability to discipline Saudi Arabia, punish it, and force it out of the game in the fields of oil and the economy."

articles.title: Trump says Ukraine, Russia 'going to make a deal,' discusses Patriot missile production
articles.body:
Merve Aydogan
22 September 2026•Update: 22 September 2026
US President Donald Trump said he believes a deal between Ukraine and Russia is imminent as he held a meeting Tuesday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly's high-level week in New York.
"We have a very good relationship going, the two of us. The president (Zelenskyy) and I are trying to figure out the solution, and I think it's going to happen. I really do," said Trump. "But the relationship is very strong, and with Europe it's very strong. And you saw what just happened with Greenland, which was something very special.”
Asked whether he still believed Ukraine could reclaim all its territory, Trump said, "Well, I think they're going to make a deal, and I don't want to say what the deal is. We talk about it a lot, including with President (Vladimir) Putin, and I think something's going to happen."
"But, certainly they are very good fighters. Really, they could be proud of themselves," he said, calling Ukraine's leadership "very capable."
Pointing to Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refining capacity, Trump said, "The strikes inside Russia on the refining capacity and the diesel, it seems like that's been a serious hit on the Russians. It's also a serious hit on the price of diesel."
"I think they (Putin and Zelenskyy) both want to see the war end. To be honest with you, it's time. A lot of people being killed, and they don't want that," said Trump.
On possible Patriot missile production in Ukraine, Trump said, "We're talking about that. We'll be talking about that now,” he said. “Very capable production. I mean, we talk about it all the time. Very capable people. Really amazingly capable people."
Zelenskyy said he hoped "we will end this war, and President Trump will help us to end this war," adding it was needed "as quick as possible before winter."

articles.title: Iran denies dropping preconditions amid ‘very productive’ three-hour UN talks in New York
articles.body:
Iran has pushed back on claims that it dropped former preconditions for reopening the strait of Hormuz in surprise talks held in New York under the mediation of Qatar between Tehran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Trump said the three-hour talks held in a room at the UN headquarters had gone very well and been very productive. He suggested further talks were possible imminently, which led to the price of a barrel of Brent crude to fall to below $100 (£75) for the first time in two weeks. Witkoff said the talks had been “encouraging, constructive and successful”.
In his speech to the UN general assembly, Trump said he had a decision to make very soon on whether to “annihilate the Islamic Republic” or help turn it into one of the great countries of the Middle East, the kind of bombastic threat Trump often deploys during talks with Iran.
In Tehran, the foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmail Baghaei, confirmed the talks had occurred, but appeared not to confirm any shift in the Iranian negotiating position. He said: “The interaction that took place with the American side was through Qatari mediation. This interaction was aimed at conveying Iran’s conditions, including the end of the war in all its dimensions, the cessation of American aggressive actions, the naval siege, and the economic war, the release of Iranian assets and so on.” Aware of the potential domestic backlash, he added that Iran’s conditions had been conveyed.
Iran set seven preconditions before returning to talks, and in a new development over the past 48 hours said the crucial strait of Hormuz could be reopened within seven days if those conditions were met.
It is likely that the US and the Gulf states would have to accept a navigational route for shipping in the strait of Hormuz – a key waterway for transporting oil – that requires commercial shipping to enter through a sea lane mainly in Iranian waters and under Iranian rather than Omani control.
The fact that the talks lasted three hours suggests some progress was made. The US side is under pressure to leverage down oil prices and increase the availability of refined oil before the midterm elections in November. Latest published figures suggest the number of identifiable tankers making it through the strait is fewer than five a day, but estimates of the US navy are much higher.
The blockage in the strait is made worse by the uncertainty surrounding the control by the Houthis’ (the Iranian-backed Yemeni paramilitaries) of a second energy transport chokepoint, the Bab al-Mandab strait that leads from the Red Sea into the Indian Ocean.
There is little sign that Trump wants to relaunch a full-scale war with Iran or indeed with the Houthis as Republicans battle to turn the domestic political agenda away from a hugely unpopular war that the Americans think they are losing.
Iran is under ever more intense pressure from sanctions, and a US naval blockade is making it nearly impossible for Iran to export oil, depriving the country of badly needed foreign currency. Iran’s civilian aircraft on Wednesday faced a potential worldwide grounding owing to the threat of US secondary sanctions on any entity that engaged with Iran’s civilian fleet.
Iranian officials negotiated frantically with neighbouring countries to try to maintain an air bridge, but it appears Oman and Iraq have been forced to close their airspace to Iranian civilian planes.
The president of Iran, Masoud Pezeshkian, is due to address the UN general assembly on Wednesday after arriving in New York on a flight from Tehran as talks were under way.
Pezeshkian is an advocate of negotiations with the US but has not played a direct role in the talks. He has said the memorandum of understanding (MoU), agreed with the US on 17 June, remained the starting point.
Implementation of the MoU fell apart after the two sides accused one another of breaching its terms by trying to take control of the strait. Iran said the MoU clearly left Iran in control of the strait for an interim period before a long-term agreement on its management was reached, including the possibility of Oman and Iran charging fees for navigational services.
Pezeshkian is expected to condemn western double standards over what he regards as an illegal US assault on Iran that has left schoolchildren dead and infrastructure ravaged. Europe’s preparedness to call out Russia for its invasion of Ukraine, and its reticence in criticising the attack on Iran, or Israel’s treatment of Palestinians in Gaza, has been a constant theme of Pezeshkian’s remarks.
Many of the most powerful speeches on Tuesday at the UN general assembly came from European and Arab politicians who decried the inability of the west to enforce peace. In his farewell speech to the UN, the French president, Emmanuel Macron, criticised the attempt to overthrow the Iranian government by the US and Israel, arguing: “Every time a few states, sometimes even in the name of international order, have tried to replace the people in order to change a regime or a system, they have plunged those states into even greater chaos.”
He also said that the west had not imposed a peace in Gaza. “Some boast of a supposed peace. But this peace hasn’t reopened humanitarian routes for a single second. Must we stand by and watch this spectacle that shames us all? Never!”
Macron landed himself in hot water with Israel when he suggested Hamas was not present in the West Bank, as opposed to Gaza.
Netanyahu’s office responded, using the biblical name for the West Bank: “Hamas terrorists carry out attacks against Jews almost every day. They have murdered countless Israeli civilians in Judea and Samaria.”
Jordan’s King Abdullah II attacked the Israeli government for “moving the goalposts”, for continuing attacks and the destruction of civilian infrastructure in Gaza, and for refusing to withdraw from the war-torn Palestinian territory. This has forced the Palestinian population in Gaza into barely one-third of the territory, he said.
Observers must no longer treat Israeli policies as “temporary military measures” or a “consequence of war”, he said.
“Accountability begins when we call things what they are: an attempt to erase Palestinian life and impose a new territorial reality in Gaza,” he added.

articles.title: Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Command Posts, Rubicon Depot in the Donetsk, Luhansk Region
articles.body:
Ukraine’s Armed Forces struck several Russian military targets in eastern Ukraine on Tuesday and overnight into Wednesday, including drone command posts, a drone depot operated by Russia’s Rubicon unit and military logistics facilities, Ukraine’s General Staff said.
In the Donetsk region, Ukrainian forces struck Russian drone command posts near the settlements of Novoselivka Persha and Dachne, according to the statement.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Another target was a drone storage depot belonging to Rubicon near Volnovakha.
Rubicon is a specialized Russian defense ministry drone warfare center established in 2024. It is involved in combat operations, drone operator training, and the development and testing of unmanned systems. Its units operate reconnaissance and strike drones, including FPV drones, against Ukrainian forces.
Ukrainian forces also struck Russian logistics facilities.
A fuel and lubricants depot was hit near Kundriuche in the Luhansk region, while two other military supply warehouses were struck near Hirnyk and Velyka Shyshovka in the Donetsk region, the General Staff said.
Near Krasnohorivka in the Donetsk region, Ukrainian forces also struck an area where personnel from a Russian drone unit were concentrated.
Earlier strike on Russian drone site
The strikes followed a Monday Ukrainian attack on a Russian military site near Tsimbulova in Russia’s Oryol region that used to store, prepare, and launch attack drones, according to Ukraine’s General Staff.
Russian Drones Over Kyiv – War of Speed and New Deep Strike Tactics
The attack damaged at least three drone storage facilities, a launch pad for jet-powered drones, and five launchers, the General Staff said. Fires and secondary explosions were also reported at the site.
Satellite imagery published after the attack showed damage to the facility, including several struck structures and the wreckage of burned-out drones, according to analysts cited by the Telegram channel Absolutely Reliable Source.
The Ukrainian General Staff said such sites are a priority because disrupting the storage, preparation, and launch of attack drones can reduce Russia’s ability to conduct drone strikes against targets in Ukraine.

articles.title: Latvian trade mission begins in the United States, with meetings planned with global technology leaders
articles.body:
A Latvian business trade mission organised by the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA) has begun in the United States. Running alongside Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs’s working visit until 27 September, the mission covers New York, Los Angeles and San Diego. Its four sector programmes bring together representatives of start-ups, the film industry, defence and dual-use technology companies, and biomedical and pharmaceutical businesses.
“The United States is Latvia’s strategic partner and trusted ally, and this September marks 35 years since the restoration of diplomatic relations. Successful cooperation with US partners, including those in California, demonstrates the international competitiveness of Latvian companies. The delegation includes representatives of the defence and dual-use sectors, biomedicine, start-ups and the film industry. I hope this visit will help Latvian businesses establish valuable contacts in the United States and, in turn, support Latvia’s economic growth,” said President Edgars Rinkēvičs.
The first business meetings are taking place in New York and Los Angeles on Wednesday, 23 September. Over the following days, Latvian entrepreneurs will meet major US companies, investors, universities and technology transfer centres to pursue export deals, joint technology projects and investment partnerships.
“Trade between Latvia and the United States reached €1.63 billion in 2025, up 13% year on year. This is more than a strong statistical result: it is a foundation for much greater ambition. We need Latvian companies to enter US supply chains, become partners in joint product development, and attract US capital to new projects in Latvia. The United States is a strategically important economic and security partner for Latvia, and the President’s visit lends additional weight to these economic discussions. The goal is clear: new projects, orders and investment,” said Raivis Bremšmits, State Secretary at Latvia’s Ministry of Economics.
Three cities and four sector programmes
In New York, representatives of Latvia’s start-up ecosystem will meet US investors and representatives of ServiceNow, a global developer of enterprise AI and digital workflow platforms. Latvian start-ups will present their solutions at the “Pitch to a President” event, receiving feedback from US investors on their prospects in the market.
In Los Angeles, the film industry programme will begin with a meeting at Paramount. Separate programmes for Latvian defence and dual-use technology, biomedical and pharmaceutical companies are also scheduled in the city over the following days.
“Three cities, four sector programmes and dozens of carefully prepared meetings within just a few days make this one of LIAA’s largest and most complex trade missions. Its pace and scale match the ambitions of Latvian companies in the United States. Last year, Latvia’s services exports to the US rose by 10% to €510 million, with information and communications technology services accounting for more than 40% of the total. Latvian companies have the expertise and technology to sit at the same table as global leaders as equal partners. We will judge the mission’s results by the deals, joint technology projects and investments that follow these discussions,” said LIAA Director Ieva Jāgere.
Latvian delegation includes 44 companies and organisations
The trade mission includes 44 Latvian companies and organisations.
The defence and dual-use technology programme includes Aumeux, SAF North America, Origin Robotics, Raw-tech, SIA Ardlat, Perkons Energy, LMT, LMT Defence, VIC TEC and LAT Security, as well as the Latgale Special Economic Zone, the Latvian Exporters’ Association “The Red Jackets”, the Federation of Security and Defence Industries of Latvia, the Latvian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the University of Latvia and Riga Technical University.
The biomedical and pharmaceutical programme includes the National Research and Innovation Institute (NIRI), Double Helix Technologies, Rīga Stradiņš University, Riga East University Hospital, Daugavpils University and the University of Latvia.
The film industry programme includes Nafta Films, RED DOT MEDIA, Mistrus Media, Trickster Pictures, Baltic Pine Films, CINEVILLA FILMS, Ierakstu Māja and the Latvian Film Service Producers Association.
BDO Latvia and representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs are also part of the trade mission delegation. The start-up programme includes BirdyChat, Monetizr, Engycell, Submerge, Spotwise, Supliful, Tournated, Capture Study, HoneyB AI, Cellbox and Crowdable.
Los Angeles: From film studios to autonomous defence systems
On 24 September, film industry participants are scheduled to visit the Warner Bros. and HBO studios and meet representatives of Disney and Netflix. Discussions will focus on Latvia’s capabilities in film production, post-production and animation, as well as opportunities for international co-productions.
Defence and dual-use technology companies will take part in a roundtable with representatives of Southern California’s defence industry and visit Anduril, a US defence technology company developing autonomous systems and AI-based solutions. Discussions will focus on using Latvian technology in joint solutions, developing new products and bringing Latvian companies into US supply chains.
Biomedical and pharmaceutical representatives will meet economic development and life sciences organisations in Los Angeles County. They will also visit the Technology Development Group at the University of California, Los Angeles, and the Office of Technology Transfer and Corporate Partnerships at the California Institute of Technology. Discussions with researchers and technology transfer specialists will cover the commercialisation of research, joint product development and cooperation between Latvian companies and US universities.
The day will conclude with a business event hosted by the US Ambassador to Latvia at the Richard Nixon Presidential Library, bringing together the Latvian delegation and representatives of the US business community.
San Diego: Semiconductors, unmanned systems and genomics
On 25 September, the defence and dual-use technology programme will continue in San Diego, a major US centre for defence, aviation and unmanned systems technology.
Latvian companies are scheduled to meet Shield AI, a developer of autonomous aircraft and AI pilot technology, and Kratos, a national security technology company active in unmanned systems, space, hypersonics and missile propulsion. Meetings are also planned with Qualcomm, a global communications, connectivity and semiconductor company; public safety technology company Axon; and Starling Systems.
Representatives of SAF Tehnika and Riga Technical University will meet senior executives at Analog Devices. The global semiconductor company has more than 100,000 customers and reported revenue of $11 billion in its 2025 fiscal year.
“SAF Tehnika regularly takes part in LIAA trade missions to the United States because they allow us to meet senior executives at partner and customer companies and strengthen our reputation with them. For example, during this September’s mission to California, we and Riga Technical University will meet the senior management of a major US semiconductor manufacturer. Opportunities like those offered by LIAA produce results only when a company has done its homework and can say precisely whom it wants to meet and what it hopes to achieve. If you don’t know where you’re going, any road will do,” said Jānis Bergs, Member of the Board and Vice President of Sales and Marketing at SAF Tehnika.
In San Diego, biomedical and pharmaceutical companies will meet Thermo Fisher Scientific, one of the world’s largest suppliers of laboratory, life sciences and pharmaceutical technologies, with annual revenue exceeding $45 billion. Meetings are also planned with Illumina, a leading developer of genomics and DNA sequencing technologies, and DNA sequencing technology company Element Biosciences.
The Latvian delegation will also visit the Technology Transfer Office at San Diego State University and the Office of Innovation and Commercialization at the University of California, San Diego, to discuss research cooperation, technology transfer and bringing new biomedical products to market.
LIAA organises participation in overseas trade missions under the EU co-financed Innovative Entrepreneurship Development Programme for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs), supported by the European Regional Development Fund and national funding. Companies may participate either on a paid basis or with support to cover eligible costs.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: There is a high risk of attack on European countries; they must respond
articles.body:
Zelenskyy: There is a high risk of attack on European countries; they must respond
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy believes there is a high risk of Russia attacking European countries.
Source: Zelenskyy's answers to journalists after his meeting with Trump
Details: Zelenskyy said that, in his view, it was important for Putin to demonstrate certain results of the war to Russian society.
Quote: "It's not about us, not about Americans, not about Ukrainians. He doesn't respect anybody. His [Putin's] main issue is the Russian people, his internal society, and pressure. He fears only his nation. That's why when you have one million people on the battlefield, on the territory of another country, who are dying – 32,000, 33,000 per month – how can you explain what it is for, if you don't have any victories?"
Details: Zelenskyy believes that this is why Putin wants to break the unity between European countries or between Europe and the US in order to reduce support for Ukraine and increase pressure.
Quote: "How to divide the unity in Europe? If we build what we didn't have before the war, but we built it together. How to do it? To attack somebody else? To strike and say, 'Look, I will go further if you don't stop this'.
To do this or really to divide societies in Europe when societies will be afraid. What he's doing now, with drones attacking Moldova, Romania, crossing borders of Poland, Germany airports, Nordic countries. So he will continue doing this.
That's why the risk of an offensive by drones, missiles, or land operations is very high against other countries bordering Russia or Belarus."
"What would they have to do? Respond. Always respond. It's not about the war. If you don't respond to Russians, they will go further."
Background: Zelenskyy said at a press conference after talks with US President Donald Trump that he is ready to meet Russian leader Vladimir Putin and that the White House could help organise a trilateral meeting.

articles.title: How is the US trying to ground Iranian airlines worldwide?
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Inside Trump's bid to shut Iran out of global aviation
The US has issued an ultimatum to countries and companies continuing to provide services to Iranian airlines.
In the latest salvo under the Trump administration's "Operation Economic Outcast", Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has announced that organisations that continue to have ties to the country's airlines after Wednesday risk being frozen out of the global financial system.
Here's what we know about Washington's bid to shut Iranian airlines out of international aviation.
What has the US done?
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said this week that, from 23 September, the US will impose secondary sanctions on airports and aviation service companies that continue to work with Iranian airlines.
Companies that continue to deal with Iranian carriers after this date risk being locked out of the dollar-based financial system.
That includes airport operators, cargo service providers, ground handlers and fuel suppliers.
"On 23 September all Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world," Bessent told CNBC.
"How do we do that? That if they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets, or you will be knocked out of the dollar system," he said.
This follows a decision by the Treasury on 8 September to slap sanctions on 27 Iranian airlines and another nine aviation service companies.
"Let this be a warning to anyone doing business with Iran's remaining airlines: You are at risk of being cut off from the global financial system," Bessent said at the time.
How have countries responded?
Several countries have announced restrictions in the days since the sanctions were announced.
Mahan Air announced it had suspended flights to Istanbul and Ankara at the request of Turkish authorities on 21 September. A few days earlier, the carrier halted its Tehran-Muscat route.
Georgia has also introduced a blanket ban on Iranian carriers using the country's aviation sector.
Meanwhile, AFP reported that Iraq is expected to comply with the US measures, citing several sources, including a senior Iraqi government official.
However, Baghdad had not formally announced the restrictions as of Tuesday, while online flight data seen by The New Arab continued to show Iranian-operated flights available to Baghdad and Najaf.
The uncertainty has already caused disruption for Iraqi travel agencies, particularly in Najaf, where many businesses depend heavily on flights carrying pilgrims between Iraq and Iran.
Some agencies have stopped taking flight bookings or begun switching customers to land routes, while others have warned that the restrictions could cause major losses. Travelling overland can also significantly increase journey times, particularly for elderly passengers and Iraqis travelling to Iran for medical treatment. A journey to the holy city of Qom, for example, can take more than 12 hours from the border.
Mahan Air routes to key countries, including the United Arab Emirates, China, Russia, India, Pakistan and Thailand, also do not appear to have been affected so far.
Beijing sharply criticised the measures as "illegal".
"China consistently opposes illegal unilateral sanctions that lack a basis in international law or authorisation from the UN Security Council," foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters.
How will this impact Iran's aviation industry?
Iran's aviation industry has already been severely degraded after years of US sanctions that have made it extremely difficult to modernise and maintain its ageing civilian aircraft fleet.
Airlines have struggled to obtain crucial spare parts and components needed for repairs and maintenance, raising longstanding concerns about the safety and reliability of the country's ageing aircraft.
The impact of the latest measures will depend largely on how many countries and aviation companies comply with Washington's threat of secondary sanctions.
The most immediate effects will be felt by carriers operating international routes. The bulk of Iran's overseas routes are handled by three airlines - state-owned flag carrier Iran Air, Mahan Air and Qeshm Air - while smaller carriers operate short-haul routes to Iraq and Gulf countries.
If airports, fuel suppliers, ground handlers and ticketing companies comply with the US measures, Iranian carriers could find it increasingly difficult to operate abroad even in countries that have not formally banned them.
Why is the US doing this?
The sanctions are part of the Trump administration's so-called "economic D-Day", which aims to further isolate Iran from the global economy.
Aviation was among five sectors the administration said Tehran was using to circumvent existing US sanctions, move money and provide military support to its allies in the region.
"Iran continues to use its supposed 'commercial' airlines, many of which are controlled by the regime and the IRGC, to ferry fighters, ship weapons and sensitive technologies, and move gold and hard cash to its proxies," the Treasury wrote.
The return to economic pressure comes amid continued deadlock after almost seven months of war.
Concerns about munitions stockpiles, souring public opinion and limited military options have left the White House hesitant to return to open conflict but unwilling to negotiate a peace deal.
The deadlock comes at a particularly sensitive time for Trump, less than two months before the crucial US midterm elections, with polls showing declining public support for both the war and his presidency.
